name: Nemea
description: Agiorgitiko from the Peloponnese, grown where Heracles killed the Nemean lion: soft, dark-fruited and velvety, Greece's most approachable serious red.
funFact: Agiorgitiko means 'St George's grape', and Nemea's wine is nicknamed the Blood of Heracles after the lion he strangled in the same valley — Greek wine names tend to come with mythology attached.

serve.how: Serve slightly cool in a large glass. Agiorgitiko has naturally low acidity and soft tannin, so over-warming makes it flabby — keep it below room temperature. High-altitude Nemea bottlings are firmer and repay a short decant; valley-floor wines are best drunk young and simply.

composition.summary: Soft, dark-fruited Agiorgitiko from a high valley in the Peloponnese.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Agiorgitiko.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Nemea appellation in the northern Peloponnese, from valley floor to 900 metres.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with moderate extraction.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in French and American oak.

composition.process: A wide altitude range within one appellation gives everything from soft valley wines to structured mountain bottlings, with oak ageing rounding the naturally supple tannin.

name: Naoussa
description: Xinomavro from northern Greece — pale, savagely tannic and high in acid, with tomato and olive notes that make comparisons to Barolo inevitable.
funFact: Xinomavro means 'acid black', and its combination of pale colour with ferocious tannin and high acidity leads almost every taster to reach for the Nebbiolo comparison eventually.

serve.how: Decant young bottles for at least an hour — young Xinomavro is genuinely austere and needs the air. Serve cool in a large glass. Do not judge it by colour; it is pale to the point of looking weak while being one of the most tannic wines in Europe. Ten years in bottle transforms it.

composition.summary: High-acid, high-tannin Xinomavro from the slopes of Mount Vermio.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Xinomavro.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Naoussa appellation on the eastern slopes of Mount Vermio in Greek Macedonia.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with extended maceration.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in oak, traditionally large neutral casks.

composition.process: A cool continental site holds acidity extremely high while long maceration extracts formidable tannin, producing wines built almost entirely for long ageing.

name: Santorini
description: Assyrtiko from volcanic ash, on vines trained into ground-level baskets to survive the wind. Searing acidity, salt and smoke, with almost no rain all year.
funFact: Santorini's vines are woven into low basket shapes called kouloura that shelter the fruit inside from wind and sun, and because the island never had phylloxera, many root systems are centuries old.

serve.how: Serve chilled but not ice-cold; the salinity and smoke need a few degrees to show. Use a standard white glass. Santorini Assyrtiko has unusually high alcohol for a wine this acidic, so it stands up to rich seafood far better than its citrus profile suggests. It also ages well for a decade.

composition.summary: Volcanic, high-acid Assyrtiko from ancient basket-trained vines on a windswept island.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Assyrtiko, with Athiri and Aidani.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Santorini in the Cyclades, on volcanic ash and pumice with almost no rainfall.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Cool stainless fermentation, fermented bone dry.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Usually unoaked; some producers use old barrels or extended lees ageing.

composition.process: Vines survive on sea mist rather than rain, and volcanic soils with extreme sun give wines of high alcohol and ferocious acidity at the same time.

name: Bekaa Valley
description: Rhône and Bordeaux varieties grown at a thousand metres in a high valley between two mountain ranges, in a wine culture older than most of Europe's.
funFact: Château Musar continued making wine through most of the Lebanese civil war, moving grapes across active front lines to reach the winery — production was missed in only two vintages, 1976 and 1984.

serve.how: Decant young bottles for an hour. Serve cool in a large glass. Traditional Bekaa reds are made in an oxidative, long-aged style that can read as unusual if you expect modern fruit — that character is deliberate. Older bottles often show better than young ones and are worth seeking.

composition.summary: High-altitude Mediterranean reds blending Rhône and Bordeaux varieties.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cinsault, Carignan, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Grenache.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Bekaa Valley at around 1,000 metres, between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Warm fermentation, in the traditional houses with long maceration.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–36 months in oak, with extended bottle age before release.

composition.process: High altitude keeps acidity intact under intense Mediterranean sun, and long oak and bottle ageing produce the savoury, dried-fruit style the valley is known for.

name: Upper Galilee
description: Israel's premium red district on the volcanic slopes below Mount Hermon — cool nights, high elevation, and Bordeaux varieties with a Mediterranean herbal edge.
funFact: Israeli winemaking was effectively restarted in the 1880s with Rothschild backing and French rootstock, then transformed again in the 1980s when growers moved into the cool high Galilee.

serve.how: Serve cool in a large glass and decant young bottles for around forty minutes. The herbal, minty edge is a regional signature from the altitude and the scrubland around the vineyards. Check whether a bottle is kosher and mevushal — flash-pasteurised wines are made differently and taste it.

composition.summary: Cool, high-elevation Bordeaux varieties on volcanic and limestone soils.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Franc.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Upper Galilee and Golan slopes, at 400–1,200 metres below Mount Hermon.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with controlled extraction.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in French oak.

composition.process: Altitude and cold nights slow ripening in a hot country, retaining acidity, while volcanic soils and Mediterranean scrub give the wines their herbal signature.

name: Judean Hills
description: Terraced limestone hills outside Jerusalem, replanted on terraces that have held vines on and off since antiquity — leaner and stonier than the Galilee.
funFact: Ancient winepresses cut directly into the limestone bedrock are scattered across these hills, and some modern vineyards are planted on terraces built two thousand years ago.

serve.how: Serve cool in a large glass. These are generally leaner and more mineral than Galilee wines, so avoid over-extracting them with a long decant — twenty to thirty minutes is enough. The stony, herbal profile suits simply grilled food better than heavily sauced dishes.

composition.summary: Limestone-terraced Mediterranean reds in the hills around Jerusalem.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot and increasingly Mediterranean varieties.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Judean Hills west of Jerusalem, on terraced limestone at 400–900 metres.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented with moderate extraction to preserve freshness.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in French oak.

composition.process: Free-draining limestone and hillside elevation restrict vigour and hold acidity, producing wines that are stonier and more restrained than Israel's warmer districts.

name: Cappadocia
description: Indigenous Anatolian varieties grown on volcanic tuff at 1,200 metres, in a region where wine has been made continuously for thousands of years.
funFact: Turkey has one of the largest vineyard areas on earth but turns only a small fraction of it into wine — most of the crop goes to table grapes and raisins, a legacy of the country's drinking laws.

serve.how: Serve slightly cool in a large glass. Native varieties like Kalecik Karası are light and aromatic and behave more like Pinot Noir than like a Mediterranean red, so do not over-warm or over-decant them. Öküzgözü and Boğazkere blends are firmer and take a longer decant.

composition.summary: High-altitude indigenous Anatolian reds on volcanic tuff soils.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Kalecik Karası, Öküzgözü, Boğazkere and Emir for whites.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Cappadocia in central Anatolia, at around 1,000–1,300 metres on volcanic tuff.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented at moderate temperature to preserve aromatics.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in oak, often neutral.

composition.process: High-altitude continental conditions with hot days and cold nights ripen native varieties while retaining the bright acidity that defines the regional style.

name: Guerrouane
description: Morocco's best-known appellation, on the plateau below the Atlas mountains — pale, dry gris rosé built to be drunk very cold with spiced food.
funFact: Morocco was once among France's largest wine suppliers, and its vineyards were largely uprooted after independence; the surviving appellations around Meknès still work to a French AOC-style system.

serve.how: Serve very cold in a white wine glass rather than a large bowl. Moroccan gris is paler and drier than Provence rosé and made specifically to cut through spiced food, so pair it with tagine or grilled meat rather than treating it as an aperitif. Drink the current vintage only.

composition.summary: Pale dry gris rosé from Rhône varieties on a high plateau below the Atlas.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cinsault, Grenache and Carignan.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Guerrouane appellation near Meknès, on a plateau at around 600 metres.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Direct pressing for very pale colour, cool stainless fermentation.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: No oak; bottled young for immediate drinking.

composition.process: Altitude moderates a hot climate enough to retain acidity, and direct pressing with cool fermentation gives a very pale, dry and deliberately refreshing style.
